result.headline: No strong cause was found; the service measures well here [speed_cell][speed_neighbours].
result.explanation: The cell averages 133.6 Mbps download from 1425 tests, above the UK median of 103 Mbps [speed_cell]. Nearby cells average 148.8 Mbps [speed_neighbours]. Sites for EE, O2 and Vodafone are about 0.1 km east with clear lines of sight [los_ee][los_o2][los_vodafone], and Three's site is about 0.2 km south with a line that only just clears the ground [los_three]. All four operators have sites within 5 km [operators_5km]. There is no severe weather or active warning [weather][met_office_warnings].

hypotheses.explanation: The cell measures well above the UK median with 1425 tests [speed_cell], and nearby cells are similar [speed_neighbours], so no persistent signal problem is shown at this point. Sites are close with clear lines for EE, O2 and Vodafone [los_ee][los_o2][los_vodafone], all four operators have sites within 5 km [operators_5km], and there is no severe weather or active warning [weather][met_office_warnings]. The only marginal item is Three's near-ground line [los_three], which is weak evidence and cannot establish a cause.

history.reason: critic: The belief claims no persistent signal problem, but the prior diagnosis (same location) concluded terrain blocking for Three. While prior_diagnoses is not independent evidence, it flags a contradiction that the belief dismisses without addressing. The aggregate speed tests [speed_cell][speed_1km][speed_neighbours] are strong but mask operator-specific issues; Three's marginal line of sight [los_three] (weak, assumed antenna height) remains a plausible cause for Three users. Confidence 0.90 overstates certainty given this operator-specific gap.

rule_based.label: Based on data, not yet reviewed by agents
rule_based.rule: Operators ranked by line of sight from this point to their nearest identified site (clear, then marginal, then blocked); clear lines by distance, obstructed ones by how far the ground rises above the line.
rule_based.text: Likely best network here: Vodafone, with a clear line of sight to a site 0.1 km east (confirmed by Ofcom's licence register). Also a clear line: EE (0.1 km), O2 (0.1 km) and Three (0.2 km).

limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed for Three; Ofcom figures are area-level.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.
